headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0053 — The computer didn't let SMTO control that app or window

html:
SMTO-EXE-0053 — The computer didn't let SMTO control that app or window

GUID: 28531824-7589-57d5-b9a5-2091225425ce
Slug: desktop-permission-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • The operating system on the Gateway computer refused SMTO's request to see or control an app or window. On a Mac this usually means the Gateway lacks Accessibility permission. Part of the action may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On a Mac, open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility on the Gateway computer and turn on access for the Gateway, or for the app that starts it. macOS blocks one program from controlling others until it is given this permission.
  2. Make sure the app you want controlled is running for the same signed-in user as the Gateway, not as an administrator or another user. The system refuses control of windows owned by other accounts or running with higher rights.
  3. Look at the app or window on that computer to see whether the action, such as close or quit, already happened. Some refusals arrive after the request was sent, so the change may be partly done.
  4. Ask SMTO again only if the action still hasn't happened. This avoids doing the same thing twice, such as closing a second window.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists the windows on that computer and the requested action completes as expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't run the Gateway as an administrator or turn off system security to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A native desktop API refused application/window access or an action (macOS Accessibility not trusted or AX error -25211, app terminate refused, or a Win32 EnumWindows/PostMessage/ShowWindowAsync/SetWindowPos failure); some refusals may follow a partial effect.

What this means

  • Native desktop APIs refused application/window access or action, or macOS Accessibility trust was absent. Some action failures retain possible effects. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Native desktop APIs refused application/window access or action, or macOS Accessibility trust was absent. Some action failures retain possible effects.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the Gateway's OS account and platform permission state, then inspect retained effect certainty for any attempted action.

How to fix it

  • On macOS grant the Gateway process Accessibility trust (AXIsProcessTrusted) in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility; on Windows run the Gateway in the target window's interactive session at a matching privilege level. Before any further mutation, observe the target's current state with desktop.windows or desktop.applications, because effect_unknown may be true.
  • Grant the Gateway Accessibility permission on macOS or use a session with access to the target window.

Retry and execution caution

  • Grant the Gateway Accessibility permission on macOS or use a session with access to the target window.

How to verify the fix

  • Required permission is deliberately granted and the original action state is known before further mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
